message.title: Can Intel's Core Ultra Expansion With Googlebook Benefit the Stock?
message.body:
Intel Corporation INTC has extended its Core Ultra platform to new Googlebook laptops from Alphabet Inc. GOOGL powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors. Developed with Google, the new laptops are being brought to market by PC makers Acer, ASUS and Lenovo, combining Intel processing and connectivity technologies with Google's computing experience.Intel's latest processors deliver responsive performance and power efficiency for modern computing. Built on its advanced 18A process technology, the Core Ultra Series 3 integrates CPU, GPU and NPU architectures to support demanding workloads and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled experiences. The platform is designed to help users multitask across applications while maintaining efficient power consumption for longer battery life.The company also brings enhanced connectivity features to the new Googlebook laptops, including Intel Wi-Fi 7, Dual Intel Bluetooth 6.0 and Intel Thunderbolt. These technologies deliver fast and reliable connections across different environments while supporting seamless device experiences.Building on more than a decade of collaboration between Intel and Google, the launch introduces premium laptops with modern designs, vibrant displays and next-generation features. The initiative supports Intel's efforts to deliver high-performance, efficient and AI-capable technologies across a broader range of devices.

How Are Competitors Performing in the PC Market?

Intel faces competition from Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM and Advanced Micro Devices AMD. Qualcomm is strengthening its presence in the PC market with its Snapdragon X2 processors, which offer AI capabilities, performance and power efficiency. The company launched the Snapdragon C platform for affordable laptops targeting students, families and small businesses. Qualcomm is further expanding its PC portfolio through laptops from major PC manufacturers such as ASUS, HP, Lenovo and Acer.AMD is advancing in the PC market with Ryzen AI processors, which combine strong computing performance with built-in AI capabilities. The company offers Ryzen AI chips across consumer and business PCs, including laptops, desktops and workstations. AMD is working with major PC manufacturers to expand the availability of its Ryzen-powered AI PCs.

INTC's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Shares of Intel have skyrocketed 323.4% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 31.7%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Going by the price/book ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 5.96 times book value, lower than the industry average of 23.92.

INTC's earnings estimates for 2026 have increased 27.1% to $1.50 per share, while those for 2027 have increased 18.8% to $1.96 over the past 60 days.

Intel currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

novelty.reason: The prior Reference View recorded Googlebook as a planned product with unspecified Intel or Qualcomm processors. The current report newly confirms that Intel Core Ultra Series 3, built on 18A, powers the Googlebook launch with Acer, ASUS, and Lenovo.

policy.reason: The announcement confirms a product launch but provides no customer replenishment, unit sales, sell-through, supply recovery, delay, cancellation, inventory, or other specific PolicySet trigger.

expert_trade.expectation_delta: Intel is now specifically selected for a commercial Googlebook platform using Core Ultra Series 3 on 18A, with Acer, ASUS, and Lenovo bringing the laptops to market. This shifts Intel's role from an optional planned processor to an actual multi-OEM premium AI-PC launch, improving the timing and probability of client-unit, ASP/mix, and 18A product contribution. Volume and revenue are not disclosed, limiting strength but not eliminating the directional gap.
expert_trade.prior_expectation: Before this announcement, Googlebook's processor supplier was unresolved between Intel and Qualcomm, while broader Core Ultra Series 3 adoption remained largely in testing or qualification. Intel's client baseline was mixed, with Q2 client units down 8% and recovery dependent on converting OEM qualification into actual products and sustained sell-through.
expert_trade.reason: TRADE LONG: the surprise is the confirmed Intel-specific commercial stage and beneficiary shift from the prior generic Intel-or-Qualcomm plan. The launch spans a major Google platform and three OEMs, with a clear path from product availability to Intel client shipments, premium mix, and 18A validation. No unit or revenue figures are disclosed, so the edge is moderate rather than fully quantified.
